summary: Say the counting numbers in order, reaching at least 20 by age five.
Count up to 10 objects in any arrangement, one number each, and know the last number tells how many.
When asked for a number up to 5, count out exactly that many objects.
Recognize written numbers when you see them, up to at least 10.
Quickly say how many are in a small group of up to 5 things without counting.
Compare two groups of up to 10 by matching or counting, and say more, less or the same.
Act out and solve everyday adding (putting together) and taking-away problems with objects.
See the parts that make up numbers to 5, like telling how many were hidden from a group of five.
Compare two or more things by length, weight or how much they hold, using words like longer or heavier.
Start to measure how long or how full things are, by comparing or using everyday or real measuring tools.
Show data about one feature with real objects or a simple picture graph.
Sort objects by one feature on your own, say the sorting rule, then sort them again a different way.
Say where something is using words like beside, next to, between, above, below, over and under.
Name and describe flat and solid shapes, like sphere, cube and cylinder, whatever their size or turn.
Fit several shapes together on purpose to finish a shape puzzle or make a new picture.
